clue.text: Awkward steps negotiated in preparation for deal

definitions.meaning: dragging one's feet clumsily along is the gait described
mixing up a pack of cards before dealing it out

explanation.surface: A clumsy bit of footwork while getting ready to strike a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy dragging gait and the mixing of cards before dealing share the same word.

clue.text: From grotesque am I shrinking, easily frightened?

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether recoiling from a grotesque sight makes them timid.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the S of 'grotesque' to the S and H of 'shrinking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeamish means readily nauseated or upset by unpleasant sights.

clue.text: Offence generating pointlessly senseless anger

indicators.note: points are the compass letters, so a compass letter is removed from the senseless word

parts.note: numb means lacking sensation
rage is violent anger

explanation.surface: Taking offence that stirs up pointless, mindless fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointlessly' removes N, a compass point, from NUMB to leave UMB.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, feeling resentment at a slight.

clue.text: American's to tell police of clue print left by this?

parts.note: to finger someone is US slang for informing on them
a tip is a hint or clue

explanation.surface: An American informer passing a clue to police, with a print left at the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a fingerprint is left by the end of a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: The pad at the end of a finger is what leaves a fingerprint.

clue.text: Novel taking up latter part of afternoon on the radio?

definitions.text: latter part of afternoon on the radio
definitions.meaning: in the old signallers' spoken alphabet, the letters of PM were voiced as two words, and the second of them names the M

explanation.walkthrough: Old British radio and signals jargon spelt P and M as 'pip emma', so the second half of PM is the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen wrote a novel of that title, and signallers voiced the letter M with the same word.

clue.text: Important! Conservative putting forward love for intolerance

parts.note: important means big, as in a big decision

indicators.note: one letter of the party word is shifted earlier, moved up front within it

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Tory politician promoting love as the remedy for intolerance, an important announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting forward' moves the O of 'love' ahead of the T within the party word. 'Important!' looks like an exclamation but supplies a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is prejudiced refusal to accept other views, a form of narrow-minded prejudice.

clue.text: Madman needing two means of containment

parts.note: a basket is a woven container
a case is a box or container

explanation.surface: A lunatic who has to be restrained twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is informal for someone mentally unable to cope.

clue.text: Musical expert, one of many in academe

definitions.meaning: Sir George ... edited the famous Dictionary of Music and Musicians
the phrase the ... of academe describes university life

explanation.walkthrough: Sir George Grove compiled the standard dictionary of music; 'the groves of academe' is a stock phrase for scholarly life.
explanation.definitionFit: George Grove was a noted music scholar, and a cluster of trees appears in the stock phrase about universities.

clue.text: Insignificant little bottle underlies most of drug experience

indicators.note: in a down clue, the bottle piece lies below the other piece
most of means the drug word loses its last letter

parts.note: a trip is a hallucinogenic drug experience
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A tiny phial of drugs lying beneath someone's hallucinatory experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims TRIP to TRI; 'underlies' puts VIAL below it in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little importance or consequence.

clue.text: Crop that is left in yard

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the yard abbreviation

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Harvest that remains lying in the farmyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A yield is the amount produced by a harvest.

clue.text: Town-based university's right to be exclusive

parts.note: U is a standard abbreviation for university
to ban is to shut out, keeping things exclusive

explanation.surface: A city university claiming the right to keep its doors closed to outsiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban describes things belonging to a city, the opposite of rural.

clue.text: Amount of money returned by bloke snatching it — capital fellow!

indicators.note: returned means the money word is read back to front

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

indicators.note: the bloke word grabs the next piece and holds it inside

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or bloke
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man grabbing some cash handed back to him, hailed as a splendid fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the money word backwards; 'snatching' has COVE grab IT. 'capital fellow' sounds like praise but means a man from a capital city, here Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muscovite is a native of Moscow, the Russian capital city.

clue.text: Stunned maiden in a daze, wandering about:

indicators.note: the maiden letter is placed among the letters of a daze
wandering about suggests letters straying out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman so stunned she drifts around in a dazed state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M (maiden) among the letters of A DAZE, and 'wandering about' rearranges the lot. 'maiden' looks like a girl but is the cricket abbreviation: a maiden over is one where no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stunned is to be astonished or utterly astounded.

clue.text: Cured? Soldiers weren't

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
those who died no longer were, so weren't means died

explanation.surface: A question about whether wounded troops recovered, answered grimly: they didn't make it.
explanation.walkthrough: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedied means put right or healed, as an ailment is when treated.

clue.text: Shipowner favouring earlier closing around ends of June and August

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the earlier word shuts round the end letters

parts.note: prior means earlier

indicators.note: ends of picks the last letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A shipowner preferring early closing during the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of' takes E and T from 'June' and 'August'; 'closing around' puts them inside PRIOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipowner is the proprietor of a vessel, its legal owner.

clue.text: By no means quick runs into one trap

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the runs letter goes inside the trap word

parts.note: a net is a trap for fish or birds
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone slow-footed running straight into a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless and sluggish, the opposite of lively.

clue.text: Firmly established some pop music's foul

parts.note: rock is one kind of popular music, and the possessive adds its S
olid is a rare word meaning foul-smelling or rank

explanation.surface: A judgement that some pop music is firmly established and also rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: OLID is a rare dictionary word for foul-smelling; the possessive 's on 'music's' supplies an S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rock-solid is utterly stable and dependable, firmly settled in place.

clue.text: Modern composer raising passions with a record

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the passions word is read upward, so backwards

parts.note: ires are angers, strong passions
a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A contemporary composer stirring emotions with an album.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns IRES upward into SERI in this down answer. Serialism is twelve-tone composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A serialist composes music using the twentieth-century twelve-tone technique.

clue.text: Study? It's an attempt to attain medical discipline

parts.note: a den is a study or private room
'tis is an old contraction of it is
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Studying hard is how one tries to master a branch of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentistry is the branch of medicine dealing with teeth.

clue.text: These help to water hard round seed in spots

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the seed word sits inside the spots word

parts.note: spots as a verb means sees, catches sight of
a pip is a small seed in fruit

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: watering devices work hard around seeds planted in patches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' reads as a noun, patches of ground, but is the verb meaning sees.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden hoses carry water to plants, so they help with watering.

clue.text: Calls out for dishevelled hiker to get on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard ship, so the scrambled walker goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the ship one boards

indicators.note: dishevelled means untidy, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Shouts telling a scruffy rambler to climb aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishevelled' rearranges the walker's letters, and 'on board' puts them inside SS, steamship: being on board a ship is a stock container idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrieks are high-pitched cries, things screamed out.

clue.text: Tree Roman turned over in the middle

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is flipped upside down, which changes its shape into another letter

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier rolling over at the halfway point of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of ROMAN is M; turned upside down it becomes W.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan is the mountain ash, a small tree with red berries.

clue.text: What's left of the road, perhaps?

definitions.text: What's left of the road, perhaps?

parts.words: What's left of the road, perhaps?
parts.note: reads as the remains of a ruined road, but means the strip beside it, perhaps the left-hand verge

explanation.definitionFit: The verge or edge beside a road is one of its sides, and in Britain traffic keeps to the left.

clue.text: Mixed vegetable in soil with disease, in which one's planted

parts.note: mire is muddy soil or bog

indicators.note: the one letter is set into the disease word like a seedling in earth

parts.note: pox is a disease, as in smallpox
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Growing vegetables in diseased soil, with one specimen planted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted' puts I inside POX to make POIX.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirepoix is a cooking base of diced mixed vegetables such as carrot, onion and celery.

clue.text: Hot food found first in this part of Ireland

indicators.note: the food word is found ahead of the hot letter

parts.note: meat is food
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Hot food discovered first in a particular Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: MEATH is a county of Ireland, north-west of Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Meath is a county in the east of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Ring including Rheingold. finally as part of cycle

indicators.note: the ring word holds the next piece inside

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring cycle, with Das Rheingold the final part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Wagner's Ring cycle, whose first opera is Das Rheingold; the cycle here is a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal is the foot lever on a bicycle.

clue.text: Old documents showing extremes of poverty in most of capital

indicators.note: the poverty letters go inside the shortened capital
most of means the capital's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Historical records revealing pockets of poverty in most of a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts PARIS to PARI; 'extremes of' takes P and Y from 'poverty', which go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyri are ancient manuscripts written on reed paper from Egypt.

clue.text: Messy chap upset dishes, dropping one in middle

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, so read backwards
the central letter of the dishes word is removed

parts.note: bowls are dishes

explanation.surface: A clumsy fellow knocks over the dishes and drops one in the middle of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping one in middle' removes W from BOWLS; 'upset' turns BOLS over.
explanation.definitionFit: A slob is a lazy, untidy person.

clue.text: Tale can spread wildly about party, based on brief account

indicators.note: the scrambled letters wrap around the party word
spread wildly signals the letters of tale can scattered into a new order

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A story that can spread wildly about a party, resting on hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread wildly' makes ANECTAL from TALE CAN, and 'about' wraps it round DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence rests on short personal stories rather than systematic data.

clue.text: Dupe — one in party is into it

indicators.note: the combined piece goes inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the one letter goes inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fool at a party who is really into it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'in' and 'into' each put one piece inside another. 'party' is DO, a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dupe is someone easily fooled, a gullible simpleton.

clue.text: Dubious operator not entirely ruthless, having reformed

indicators.note: having reformed signals the letters are re-formed into a new order
not entirely means the word ruthless loses one letter at its end

explanation.surface: A shady character, not completely ruthless, who has mended his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the last S of RUTHLESS; 'having reformed' rearranges RUTHLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustler is a con artist or swindler, someone working shady deals.

clue.text: A lot of chickens, and how they came when fried?

definitions.meaning: a large group of hens kept in rows of cages for egg production
coated in batter, as fried chicken may be served

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition treats the word as an adjective of batter, meaning coated in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensively farmed hens are kept in cage systems, and battered food is coated before frying.
